en: The Philippine eagle, our national bird, boasts a wingspan of up to two meters, making it one of the largest rare eagles globally.
The Philippines declared independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, ending exactly 333 years of Spanish colonial rule that began in 1565.
The Philippine Senate, the upper house of Congress, is composed of exactly 24 senators who are elected nationally for six-year terms.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct living languages, but the 1987 Constitution designates only Filipino and English as official languages.
The annual Sinulog Festival in Cebu attracts over two million attendees, making it one of the largest cultural festivals in the country.
The Lumad comprise 18 distinct ethnolinguistic groups in Mindanao, collectively representing about 15 percent of the total indigenous population nationally.
National hero Jose Rizal was only 35 years old when he was executed by firing squad on December 30, 1896.
Under Philippine law, citizens must be at least 18 years old to vote, allowing over 65 million Filipinos to participate in 2022 elections.
The national gem, the Philippine Pearl, can grow up to 20 millimeters in diameter, making it the largest cultured pearl globally.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School in 1936 and established the country's first pediatric hospital in 1957.
The Philippines is politically divided into exactly 81 provinces, which are grouped into 17 different administrative regions, including the National Capital Region.
The San Juanico Bridge, the longest bridge in the Philippines, spans exactly 2.16 kilometers across the strait, connecting Leyte and Samar.
